analysis.headline: Stocks fell Tuesday (S&P 500 down about 1% to its lowest close since July, Dow down about 849 points, Nasdaq down 0.7%), but futures are higher this morning after Nvidia's results beat expectations.
analysis.summary: Tuesday's selloff was driven by worries about AI spending and valuations ahead of Nvidia's report, plus a sharp drop in software stocks such as Salesforce after OpenAI released new models; about 17 of every 20 S&P 500 stocks fell. After the close Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier, beat earnings estimates and authorized another $150 billion in buybacks, and this morning Bloomberg had Nasdaq 100 futures up about 0.8% and S&P 500 futures up about 0.4%, on track to snap a four-day slide. Bonds remain under pressure from inflation and Fed rate-hike bets: Kitco put the 10-year Treasury yield near 5.10% and said markets are pricing further hikes, which has left gold near one-year lows around $3,850 an ounce. Oil stayed firm, with WTI settling near $86 and Brent near $93, while Bitcoin futures fell 1.4% to about $64,200, their lowest close since mid-August. Even after Nvidia's beat, one strategist told Yahoo Finance the results don't settle the bigger questions about returns on AI spending, how it is financed and leadership uncertainty after Jensen Huang's departure as CEO.
drivers: Nvidia beat third-quarter estimates ($2.68 adjusted EPS vs $2.47 expected) and gave a stronger outlook, its first report since Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO
Software stocks slid on AI-disruption fears after OpenAI released new models; Salesforce fell about 9.4%, the worst performer in the Dow and S&P 500
Rising import prices kept inflation worries alive, and futures markets are pricing a Fed rate hike at the December 8-9 meeting
A CNN report that a classified NSA communications network went down pushed the indexes to their session lows, per CNBC
watch: Today (Wed): minutes of the Oct. 27-28 Fed meeting at 2 p.m. ET (11 a.m. Pacific), plus October housing starts
Today (Wed): earnings from Target, Lowe's and TJX; Yahoo Finance reports Anthropic is preparing to price its IPO

helium.headline: North American Helium's new Stewart Valley plant is producing about 73 million cubic feet a year, and the company is pushing ahead with plans for Canada's first helium liquefier in Swift Current.
helium.summary: NAH's Stewart Valley purification facility, which the company calls Canada's largest helium field, came online on September 20, 2026 at roughly 73 million cubic feet per year, with output sold to global industrial gas distributors under long-term contracts. Its next project is a helium liquefaction plant in Swift Current, estimated at about $100 million; the company is still working toward a final investment decision and funding, and today the region's helium is trucked as gas to U.S. plants to be liquefied. A Swift Current report this week says new federal tax treatment putting helium on a footing closer to oil and gas could help the liquefier, though it is not direct funding and some of the company's requests are still under consideration. The wider market has been tight since March, when strikes halted Qatar's helium output and Russia restricted exports; analysts cited by Edison Group (including Bank of America) estimated spot prices up 40% to 100%, while long-term contract prices move more slowly.

realestate.headline: Portland-area home prices are holding roughly flat while sales have slowed sharply, with RMLS showing October's metro median at $545,000, up 0.9% from a year ago.
realestate.summary: RMLS October figures, as summarized by local brokers, show a Portland metro median sale price of $545,000 (up 0.9% year over year) while closed sales fell 21.5% from a year earlier to 1,622 and new listings dropped 12.2% to 2,077. Inventory sits at 4.3 months, which brokers describe as balanced but tilting toward buyers, and average market time was 67 days. Redfin's city-of-Portland data puts the median sale price at $525,000, up 0.9%, with homes selling in about 26 days versus 29 a year ago. Mortgage rates are easing but still high: Freddie Mac's 30-year average was 7.11% on November 12, its fourth straight weekly decline; none of today's sources broke out North Portland, St. Johns or Sauvie Island.
